Topic 2.4: Talk About

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Talk About
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: what do you learner should be able to: interactions (turn-taking, respecting like?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. use acquired vocabulary to talk others opinions) 2 lessons
2. identify themselves with people, to talk about self(name, class, age objects and places in their and gender), home, and environment community, in pairs and groups
3. demonstrate interest to use names  Learners observe the teacher of people, places, and objects modelling effective speaking skills within the environment  Learners record their speech and

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Talk About

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Talk About

Teach
• Focus skill: use acquired vocabulary to talk others opinions) 2 lessons.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Talk About.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Talk About
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. what do you learner should be able to: interactions (turn-taking, respecting like?
2. Why do you like about self appropriately  Learners engage in conversations him/her/it?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
